sources.source_title: Building the 800 VDC Ecosystem for Efficient, Scalable AI Factories

evidence_units.statement: NVIDIA proposes generating 800 VDC at the facility level and distributing it directly to 800 VDC compute racks to eliminate redundant power conversions.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Direct architectural voltage stated by NVIDIA.
exclusions: Architecture proposal; not a customer-specific deployed configuration.

limitations: Vendor-defined future architecture, not an independently verified deployment result.
Does not establish suitability for a specific customer, region, or site.

evidence_units.statement: NVIDIA states that the 800 VDC architecture is intended to scale beyond 1 MW per rack.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Threshold explicitly stated as beyond 1 MW per rack.
exclusions: Roadmap capability; not a guaranteed delivered rack rating.

limitations: Roadmap statement, not a product acceptance test or customer deployment record.

evidence_units.statement: NVIDIA states that 800 VDC alone does not address workload volatility and pairs the architecture with multi-timescale energy storage.
limitations: Does not prescribe a single storage technology, capacity, or ownership boundary.
Does not prove that every 800 VDC deployment requires the same storage topology.

evidence_units.statement: NVIDIA states that industry alignment is still required on voltage ranges, connector interfaces, and safety practices for 800 VDC environments.
limitations: Identifies unresolved ecosystem requirements; it is not proof that standards or interfaces are complete.

evidence_units.statement: NVIDIA states that the transition to a fully realized 800 VDC architecture will occur in phases.
limitations: Does not define a universal phase schedule or customer-specific deployment date.
Official vendor architecture and roadmap source, not independent benchmarking.
Performance, cost, reliability, and adoption statements must not be generalized beyond the exact evidence units.
Customer-, region-, and site-specific suitability remains unproven.

sources.source_title: Galaxy VXL 500-1250 kW UPS 380/400/415 V Technical Specifications

evidence_units.statement: The Galaxy VXL technical specification includes a 500 kW UPS rating.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Lower endpoint directly stated in the documented Galaxy VXL product rating range.
exclusions: Does not represent aggregate parallel-system capacity.
Does not independently bind the documented nominal voltage options.

limitations: Product-specific lower endpoint; must not be generalized to all UPS products.
This unit does not independently bind the documented nominal voltage options.

evidence_units.statement: The Galaxy VXL technical specification includes a 1250 kW UPS rating.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Upper endpoint directly stated in the documented Galaxy VXL product rating range.
exclusions: Does not represent aggregate parallel-system capacity.
Does not independently bind the documented nominal voltage options.

limitations: Product-specific upper endpoint; must not be generalized to all UPS products.
This unit does not independently bind the documented nominal voltage options.

evidence_units.statement: Galaxy VXL scalable models use 125 kW power modules.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Direct module rating stated in the model list.

limitations: Applies to the documented scalable Galaxy VXL models.

evidence_units.statement: A minimum of four 125 kW power modules is required for the documented scalable Galaxy VXL configuration.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Direct minimum module count stated in the model-list footnote.

limitations: Applies to the documented scalable configuration and does not define all commissioning requirements.

evidence_units.statement: For the 500 kW Galaxy VXL at 400 V and 100% load, the documented normal-operation efficiency is 97.2%.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Direct value from the efficiency table.
numeric_provenance.denominator: 500 kW model, 400 V, 100% load, normal operation
exclusions: Not eConversion, ECO, battery-operation, or partial-load efficiency.

limitations: Operating-point-specific value; must not be used as a universal Galaxy VXL efficiency.

evidence_units.statement: For the 500 kW Galaxy VXL at 400 V and 100% load, the documented eConversion efficiency is 99.4%.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Direct value from the efficiency table.
exclusions: Not normal double-conversion, ECO, battery-operation, or partial-load efficiency.

limitations: eConversion operating-point result; must not be represented as normal-operation efficiency.

evidence_units.statement: The Galaxy VXL technical specification lists an AI load tolerant UPS option as tested and validated.
limitations: The cited specification page does not disclose the complete AI load test profile, limits, or acceptance criteria.
Must not be generalized into a claim that every AI workload is supported without qualification.
Official product documentation; values apply only to documented Galaxy VXL models and operating points.
Schneider explicitly requires site-specific risk analysis and suitability evaluation.
eConversion data must not be mixed with normal double-conversion efficiency.

sources.source_title: Advanced UPS Controls for AI Workloads Management

product: UPS with Battery Shield and Input Power Smoothing controls

evidence_units.statement: Vertiv states that GPU clusters can swing from idle to full load in milliseconds.
limitations: Representative AI workload behavior; not a guaranteed profile for every GPU cluster or customer.

evidence_units.statement: Vertiv states that fast AI load transitions can cause frequent battery micro-discharges and accelerate battery aging in some UPS, depending on the load profile and system conditions.
limitations: Conditional risk statement; not proof that all UPS batteries will micro-cycle under all AI workloads.

evidence_units.statement: Vertiv states that Battery Shield can manage 0% to 100% power steps internally in the UPS without engaging the batteries.

numeric_provenance.derivation: Magnitude of the directly stated step from 0% to 100% of UPS rated load.
numeric_provenance.denominator: UPS rated load; step starts at 0% and ends at 100%
exclusions: Feature-specific claim; not a generic capability of all UPS products.
Operation above 100% and detailed test conditions require separate verification.

limitations: Applies to the described Vertiv control feature and relevant system conditions.

evidence_units.statement: Vertiv describes Input Power Smoothing as using the UPS battery system as a short-term buffer to smooth AI load peaks and stabilize UPS input power.

product: UPS with Input Power Smoothing control

limitations: Feature-specific architecture; does not define a universal buffer duration, battery duty, or upstream-grid result.
Vendor-authored technical source describing specific Vertiv control features.
Representative load profiles and laboratory statements must not be generalized to all AI loads or all UPS.
Product model, firmware, configuration, and test-condition applicability require product-level confirmation.
